newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper mixed, CFDs slightly softer.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper mixed, CFDs slightly softer.

text.p: Brent paper was steady to slightly weaker in slow early discussion on Friday while outright values retreated from early gains, traders said.
The North Sea physical crude was quiet following Thursday's firm and active market.
The front-month August Brent IPE crude contract was unchanged at $17.78 a barrel at 1031 GMT after hitting $17.91 in early business on technical strength.

Paper was mixed. Brent Contract For Differences for next week were a shade weaker at August Brent -27/-24 cents, with the following week at August Brent -30/-28 cents. The July 7-11 week was one cent adrift at -32/-29.
But 15-day intermonth paper spreads were virtually unchanged, with July/August at -17/-15 cents and August/ September at -17/-14 cents.
Traders analysing the firmer Thursday wet market attributed most of the good demand to moderate concern over the timing of a resumption in Iraqi exports.

They said Iraq's refusal to resume exports until the remaining $800 million of revenue from the first 180 days of the U.N. deal has been spent on humanitarian supplies was providing a supportive backdrop.
"I think the only reason for that level of buying has been the Iraq story," one trader said.
"But I also think that if people were really convinced that there might be no Iraqi crude until August the numbers would be a lot higher, and I don't think they are that convinced."
"I cannot imagine Iraq will allow two months to go by without shipping oil," said another trader.
